_README: Started by init.py from Dig Dug (NTSC) (Atari) (1987) (50CB13F3).a78.
Every human judgement about this ROM lives in this file; the
generated listings are disposable, so renaming is free.
What to do next, roughly in order:
Read the coverage it reports. Low coverage is normal at
first and is the number you are trying to move.
2. Every unresolved indirect jump it reports is a hole. Add the
target to `entries`, or the pointer pair to `ram_vectors` if
the handler is installed into RAM.
Finds the sound code and the tables feeding it.
4. Name things in `labels` as soon as you know what they are.
See docs/method.md for the working order and docs/pitfalls.md for
the traps that each cost real time.

comments.rom:F513: CONFIRMED, found via a PC-tagged write-tap on $2500-$25FF (tools/probe-flower-writes.lua, run-01.inp) that caught real execution inside what was an untraced gap: a per-object dispatch. LDA dat_E0B0,Y/STA ram_00D2 and LDA dat_E0B8,Y/STA ram_00D3 build a jump target from an 8-entry low/high table, then JMP (ram_00D2). disasm.py's ram_vectors scan couldn't find this on its own -- the LDA/STA pair that seeds ram_00D2/00D3 is itself inside the region only reachable through this same jump, a chicken-and-egg the scanner has no way to resolve from outside. Computed all 8 targets by hand from the raw table bytes (2 of the 8, Y=0/1, land outside plausible ROM/code space and are presumably unused slots) and added the 4 valid, distinct ones to `entries` directly -- the same trial-entry-point method method.md already documents, just applied after computing the targets from a table dump instead of guessing an address. Recovered 461 bytes of real code (44.3%->47.2%).
comments.rom:F5FB: CONFIRMED shape, found via the same probe as rom:F513: inside a per-object loop (Y counts down 7..0) that calls rom:sub_D622 (a terrain-based fall/settle check, not yet independently examined) and updates the object's position on a hit -- reads as falling-object (rock) physics. The first time a given object's EnemyStatus bit 6 is clear when it settles, writes ram_00CE (the dispatch index this whole routine was entered with) into RockOwnerSlot,Y ($2500-page; confirmed live at $2550/$2554/$2555, values 3-4) and plays a sound, then sets EnemyStatus bit 6 (a 'this object has already been counted toward its owning ObjSlot' latch, preventing re-triggering). Also checks HarpoonTargetSlot against the current object and resets it if they match (rom:sub_F7C8). REVISED, now largely disambiguated by tracing rom:sub_F6B8's tail (found afterward, see its own comment): this write does NOT itself remove the rock -- per the user's own hint ('rockfall should be just triggering the sound and disappearing'), the actual disappearance (EnemyStatus bit 6 -> bit 7, the confirmed dead/inactive bit from rom:F71C) happens later, in sub_F6B8, once the ObjSlot animation that RockOwnerSlot ties it to finishes. So this routine's real job is: on settle, tag the rock with which ObjSlot 'claimed' it and play the settle sound; the kill happens downstream. The still-open question is whether ObjSlot's animation is the level-counter flower, the veggie-appearance sequence documented at rom:sub_F513/rom:sub_F6B8, or genuinely the same thing wearing two names -- see rom:F6B8's comment for the fuller synthesis.
comments.rom:F4EF: CONFIRMED. The driver for the whole ObjSlot dispatch family (rom:sub_F513 through rom:sub_F6B8): zeroes ObjSlotActiveCount, then walks 5 slots (X=4..0 -- a pool of 5, distinct from the 8 EnemyStatus slots) calling rom:sub_F50D on each. Afterward, if ObjSlotActiveCount is back to 0 and ram_0084 (a 'pause the gated subroutines' flag also set by the player-death check at rom:F71C) is set, clears ram_0084 and sets ram_0083 -- reads as 'once no ObjSlot animation is still running, release the pause and signal something (next stage?) via ram_0083'. Not yet traced further.
comments.rom:F50D: CONFIRMED. Gate for rom:sub_F513's jump table: reads ObjSlotStage,X (the current slot's stage); if it's below 2 (idle/just-spawned), returns immediately without dispatching. Otherwise bumps ObjSlotActiveCount and falls into rom:sub_F513's jump-table dispatch using the stage value itself as the table index -- so the 4 recovered handlers (rom:sub_F522/F52A/F552/F668/F6A3, chaining into rom:sub_F6B1/F6B8) are literally 'what happens at ObjSlotStage 2, 3, 4...', a per-slot animation sequencer, not a per-object-type dispatch.
comments.rom:F6B8: CONFIRMED, and this is what disambiguates rom:F5FB. Entered at a late ObjSlotStage: reads ObjSlotRockTally,X; if zero (no rock has been attributed to this slot via RockOwnerSlot yet), just calls rom:sub_F6B1 (advances the stage, i.e. wait another cycle) and returns. Otherwise looks up dat_E0A9 by the tally value and falls into the tail: zeroes ObjSlotStage,X (ends this slot's animation) and ram_0049,X, decrements ObjSlotActiveCount, increments ram_00C8 (reset to 0 at level-init, rom:sub_D244 -- so a per-level counter), and if ram_00C8 has reached exactly 2, seeds ram_00F1=1, which rom:sub_F2E6 (elsewhere, not detailed here) drives as a step counter into a level-indexed lookup (dat_E4AA) feeding what looks like a distinct sound/graphic cue -- CANDIDATE for a jingle or on-screen flourish gated on 'the 2nd ObjSlot animation this level has completed', but the significance of exactly 2 isn't independently confirmed, only that the mechanism exists and is level-scoped. Finally, loops the 8 EnemyStatus slots and, for whichever one has RockOwnerSlot,Y == X and EnemyStatus bit 6 set, does ASL EnemyStatus,Y -- promoting the settle-latch (bit 6) into the confirmed dead/inactive bit (bit 7, rom:F71C). This is the actual rock-removal step. Combined with rom:F5FB: a rock settling only tags itself with an owning ObjSlot and plays a sound (matches the user's 'rockfall should be just triggering the sound and disappearing' -- from the player's view that's exactly what happens); the removal itself is deferred to here, piggybacking on whichever ObjSlot animation claimed it. Independently, a live PC-tagged probe on $00C5/$00FD (tools/probe-veggie-writes.lua) caught an 8-stage ObjSlotStage/ObjSlotTimer progression at ObjSlot 2 (i.e. ObjSlotStage+2/ObjSlotTimer+2) during frames 4289-4420 of run-01.inp, ending exactly at this routine's rom:F6C6, immediately followed by a score jump (2830->3240, delta 410) matching the manual's veggie point range and the user's 'I picked up a veggie once' hint. So: this same 5-slot state machine drives BOTH the visible veggie-appearance animation AND the deferred rock-removal/tally bookkeeping -- strong evidence they are the same mechanism, not two separate ones, though which specific field is 'this is a veggie' vs 'this is the level-counter flower' (the user's other hint, re end-of-level) is still not pinned down; dat_E0A9's role (a per-tally graphic/id lookup) is the most likely place that distinction lives, and is not yet decoded.
comments.rom:D057: CONFIRMED: the boot-time RAM init. Doesn't clear whole pages the way Centipede/Ballblazer's does -- clears specific, narrow ranges directly (ram_007E-0088, ram_0040-0052 paired with ram_24C0-24D2, a few ram_24C9-24D2 sub-fields) rather than one big page-sweep loop. Also copies dat_EACC/dat_C008 (both inside the confirmed chr_rom_C000/gfx_C000 region) into ram_2400,Y -- a display-list-adjacent init, not yet fully traced.
comments.rom:DF7D: CONFIRMED (SED at rom:DF80, BCD arithmetic; live-checked against tools/probe-ram-snapshots.lua, run-01.inp): the score-add routine. Adds into ScoreLo/Mid/Hi,X (X = CurrentPlayer) with carry chained across all three BCD bytes, then checks the new high-digit value (CMP #$02, AND #$0F/BEQ, CMP #$05) -- matching the manual's extra-life rule (20,000 and 50,000, then every 50,000 after: https://atariage.com/manual_html_page.php?SoftwareID=2126) almost exactly by shape, though the precise digit-place arithmetic hasn't been traced byte-by-byte. On a match, falls into rom:DF9E which increments LivesRemaining,X (capped at 10) and calls sub_DD3B (also called from the death-recovery path at rom:DC98 -- likely a shared 'lives display update' or 'life gained/restored' notification, not yet named).
comments.rom:D298: CONFIRMED: terrain/dirt map level-init. Computes LevelNumber,X (X=CurrentPlayer; confirmed as a level/round number by rom:sub_DF33's level-clear check, which increments it) mod 10 via repeated SBC #$0A, then fills a large span of TerrainMap with one of three fixed values ($20/$22/$1E) depending on the result -- a level-dependent dirt pattern. rom:sub_D2C0 (called right before, rom:D256) does a second pass: fills TerrainMap+15 through the page end with $24 (a border/edge value, matching sub_D660's own $24 threshold), then carves specific already-open cells ($4C, plus $4A into the adjacent ram_25FF page) at fixed positions from dat_E7BF (the same position table sub_D16C's display-list builder uses) -- likely the level's starting tunnel entrance(s).
comments.rom:D660: CONFIRMED: the terrain-cell classifier. Reads TerrainMap,Y and buckets it against the exact threshold values the level-init code (rom:D298) fills the map with: >= $24 (border/solid) returns a fixed $0F; < $1E (already-dug/open) returns the value halved; the $1E-$23 band (packed dirt) returns a fixed $02. Called from rom:sub_F952 in a loop stepping through cells along a movement direction -- this is collision/movement-clamping logic (how far can an object move before hitting solid terrain), not the dig action itself. The dig action is rom:sub_D8E2/rom:sub_FD43 -- see those comments.
comments.rom:C30A: CONFIRMED, found via a PC-tagged write-tap on TerrainMap (tools/probe-terrain-writes.lua, run-01.inp) that led here indirectly (see rom:D8E2): converts a pixel (X,Y) position to a TerrainMap index and reads the cell. Y-pixel >>3 (row, ram_00CC); X-pixel >>2 indexes ram_2490,X (a row-to-table-index lookup), which indexes dat_E7BF,X (the same per-row base-offset table sub_D16C's display-list builder and the level-init code both use) to get the row's TerrainMap base offset; adding ram_00CC's row-component gives the final index. `LDA TerrainMap,X` at the end reads the cell -- callers get the raw terrain byte back in A.
comments.rom:D8E2: CONFIRMED, found via a PC-tagged write-tap on TerrainMap (tools/probe-terrain-writes.lua, run-01.inp) that pointed straight at rom:sub_FD43's callers: the dig-check-and-erode routine. Looks up a movement-transition table (one of dat_E1D9/E1DD/E1CF/E1D6/..., selected by the current direction/turn state in Y) to pick which of several erosion tables (dat_E1B3/E1B7/E1BB/...) to use for this step, stores that table's pointer to ram_00CF, computes the target cell's position (rom:sub_C30A, screen position plus a per-direction offset from dat_D6F3/dat_E0DC), and -- only if the cell isn't already solid/border (CMP #$24, BCS skips the dig) -- calls rom:sub_FD43 to erode it. Checks a second, related cell the same way right after (using ram_0080 and dat_E1BB), consistent with a tunnel opening affecting more than one cell per step.
comments.rom:FD40: CONFIRMED (see rom:D8E2 for the caller chain that found this): the actual TerrainMap write-back -- `sub_FD43`'s `(old_value-$24)>>1` indexes a small lookup table (pointed to by ram_00CF, set per-direction by the caller) to get the *new* terrain value, then stores it into TerrainMap,X. This is the dig action itself: repeatedly digging the same cell walks it through a short sequence of intermediate 'partially dug' values (rather than clearing to open in one step), though the exact table contents (which values, how many steps) aren't decoded yet.
comments.rom:F952: CONFIRMED shape: per-object movement-limit check. Reads a 2-bit direction out of ram_0080 (ROR/ROR into carry+sign), then walks cells in that direction via rom:sub_D660, calling rom:sub_E1F7 (accumulates ram_009D += 4 per open cell -- a distance-so-far counter, not the dig action; a tiny 4-byte routine, easy to mistake for something bigger) for each passable cell until the classifier's bitmask test fails. Not yet confirmed which object this applies to (the player specifically, or any moving object using the same movement code) or exactly how ram_009D's accumulated distance gets used afterward.
comments.rom:F71C: CONFIRMED shape. EnemyStatus bit 7 set/negative = DEAD/inactive, not alive (see rom:DF33 for how that polarity was confirmed). Loops the 8 EnemyStatus slots; for any slot with status < 2 (i.e. not already dead or in some other state), computes the absolute X/Y pixel distance between the player (ram_0040/ram_0053) and that enemy (ram_0041,X/ram_0054,X); if both are within a small range (a proximity/collision check), sets ram_0084=1 (the main loop's own gate flag -- so this pauses the five gated subroutines, including this one, until reset), loads a death-animation graphic from dat_C155 (the exact table rom:DC41's death routine also cycles through), plays a sound, and calls rom:sub_F7C8 (resets HarpoonTargetSlot to $FF, a 'no target' sentinel -- see rom:sub_F90A). Reads as the player-touched-by-an-active-enemy death trigger.
comments.rom:F760: CONFIRMED shape, same skeleton as rom:sub_F71C but checking distance against ram_004E/ram_0061 instead of the player's own position -- a different, not yet identified reference point (a candidate for rock position, given the manual's 'drop rocks on monsters' mechanic, but not confirmed). On a hit, zeroes the enemy's EnemyStatus,X (killing it) and ram_00EF, then falls into the same ram_0084=1/sound/death-graphic sequence rom:sub_F71C uses -- consistent with a kill effect distinct from player death, sharing the same 'something notable just happened, pause and animate' plumbing.
comments.rom:D6BA: CONFIRMED, and the key that unlocked the whole harpoon mechanic: reads INPT4,Y (Y=CurrentPlayer -- the fire button) and builds FireHoldTimer, a hold-duration counter that resets to 0 the instant the button is released (BMI on INPT4 -- bit 7 clear means held, matching the usual Atari controller convention) and counts up while held, capping the behavior at exactly $18 (24) frames -- matches the manual's 'press and hold, or pump repeatedly' almost exactly. On first press, also resets HarpoonTargetSlot-adjacent state and, if a stun/transition is already in progress (rom:sub_FA33), kicks its periodic timer (ram_00B1).
comments.rom:F7F6: CONFIRMED: grows HarpoonLength by 1 each frame the harpoon is extending, but clamps it against ram_009D -- the exact distance-so-far value rom:sub_F952 computes by walking TerrainMap cells in the facing direction (via rom:sub_D660's classifier), reused here so the harpoon literally cannot extend past a wall or solid dirt. When rom:sub_F8C6 (not yet independently examined) signals the button was released, resets HarpoonLength to $FF (a 'retracted' sentinel).
comments.rom:F901: CONFIRMED: computes the harpoon tip's screen position from the player's position and HarpoonLength (scaled), with a left/right branch (rom:L_F8EA) for facing direction -- rom:sub_D6BA/rom:sub_F7F6 build HarpoonLength from the fire button; this is the position math consuming it. Falls into rom:sub_F90A, an 8-slot loop (rom:L_F90C) that checks each EnemyStatus slot's proximity to the computed tip position; on a hit, records the target in HarpoonTargetSlot, sets EnemyStatus,X = $07 (bits 0-2 all set -- the stun pattern), and sets ram_00EB = 1, the exact flag rom:sub_FA33's state machine (see that comment) checks against the current loop's X to start the stun-recovery sequence. This is the actual pump/harpoon stun hit -- found by following HarpoonLength (ram_00E2) forward from rom:sub_D6BA's fire-button read, not guessed at.
comments.rom:FA33: CONFIRMED shape, REINTERPRETED: previously read as a pure ghost-transition state machine; now clearly driven directly by the harpoon-hit flag (rom:sub_F901/rom:L_F90C sets ram_00EB=1 and EnemyStatus,X=$07 on a hit), so this is the stun-recovery sequence, and 'becomes a ghost' may be what happens if a stunned enemy is *not* finished off in time, rather than a separate, unrelated mechanic -- not yet disambiguated, but the two are connected, not coincidentally similar-shaped. EnemyStatus bits 1-2 carry the sub-state, distinct from bit 7 (dead). Bit 1 set means 'stunned/mid-sequence': a per-slot animation-stage counter (ram_2337,X) advances every time a per-slot timer (ram_233F,X) counts down to 0, and at stage 4 plays a second sound and clears bit 2 (AND #$FB) -- possibly the stun wearing off, possibly the enemy being fully digested/killed if repeatedly pumped before this fires; not yet disambiguated. Bit 1 clear checks the harpoon-hit flag (ram_00EB) and HarpoonTargetSlot (compared against the current X) before starting a new sequence -- only one enemy can be mid-sequence at a time. ram_00B1 (a periodic countdown, checked in rom:sub_F790, kicked by rom:sub_D6BA on first press) is a candidate for the ghost-conversion timer specifically, if that does turn out to be a separate path from the stun sequence -- not confirmed either way.
comments.rom:DF33: CONFIRMED: the level-clear check. Loops X=7..0 over EnemyStatus,X (bit 7 SET/negative = dead/inactive -- confirmed by this exact routine's own BPL: it exits early, level not clear, the moment it finds a slot with bit 7 clear, i.e. still alive) looking for any live one; if none are found (all 8 enemies dead), plays a sound/animation (rom:sub_FDEF, rom:sub_DD4C) then increments LevelNumber,X (X = CurrentPlayer, rom:DF4E) and re-runs the DLL setup (rom:sub_D1BE) and terrain-map init (rom:sub_D244) for the next level -- LevelNumber is exactly the ram_009B,X value rom:D298's terrain-init reads to pick the level's dirt pattern.
comments.rom:DC41: CONFIRMED LIVE (tools/probe-ram-snapshots.lua, run-01.inp): the death-handling routine. Plays a short animation loop (rom:L_DC54, cycling a sprite/character index through dat_C155 with a fixed delay), then decrements LivesRemaining,X (X = CurrentPlayer, rom:DC6F). If lives hit zero, checks the *other* player's LivesRemaining (Y = CurrentPlayer XOR 1, rom:DC85-DC8D) before deciding the game is really over (rom:sub_DD10) -- correctly handles 2-player mode not sharing a single life pool, even though this project's own recording never exercised 2-player play. If lives are still available (either this player's or, in a shared-lives 2P mode, the other's), falls through to rom:sub_DD3B instead -- the same 'life gained/restored' routine the extra-life award path calls. LIVE: LivesRemaining ($009E) counts cleanly 5->4->3->2->1->0 three separate times across the whole recording, resetting to 5 each time (frames 1980, 12540, 24300) in exact lockstep with NewGameFlag ($00A0) pulsing 0->1->0 and ScoreHi ($00A6) resetting to 0 -- a new game starting, matching the manual's '5 starting lives' exactly.
comments.rom:C15F: ENTRY_Nmi is `JMP ram_1FBD` -- NOT indirect, a plain absolute jump to a fixed RAM address. CONFIRMED self-modifying: boot code (rom:sub_D057) writes $4C (the JMP opcode itself) to ram_1FBD, then the target's low/high bytes to ram_1FBE/ram_1FBF, assembling a literal `JMP $target` instruction in RAM at $1FBD-$1FBF. Declared ram_vectors on the [ram_1FBE, ram_1FBF] pair (the scanner doesn't need to know about the fixed $4C at $1FBD -- it only tracks the two address bytes) rather than trying to special-case self-modifying code in the tool.
comments.rom:EE57: VEC_EE57, found via the ram_1FBE/1FBF ram_vectors scan. A single, self-contained multi-stage DLI handler -- not a ping-pong chain between separate routines like Centipede's. Each stage sets a WSYNC then writes a MARIA palette-color-register pair (P5C1/P5C2, P6C1/P6C3, P7C1/P7C3 -- distinct color sets, presumably per screen band) via a shared `STA ram_1FBE / BNE L_EE8E` trampoline that re-arms the *same* routine at a different internal offset for the next interrupt. This is why only one external target was found: every re-arm points back inside code already being traced, so the scan has nothing further to discover.

headers.rom:C54A: Renders cleanly at --direct 22 --lines 16 as legible bonus-point-value digit/text graphics (readable '...000' point values and what looks like a word fragment) -- NOT yet cross-checked against the manual's exact veggie/kill bonus table (400-8000 per https://atariage.com/manual_html_page.php?SoftwareID=2126). Now also confirmed live -- see the rom:C162 and rom:C362 blocks -- as part of the same graphics region this address sits inside.
headers.rom:C162: CONFIRMED, root cause found: the ~940-reference $B900-$CFFF dataset from an early pass (tools/live-slots.lua, borrowed verbatim from Centipede) was largely garbage, but not for the reason first guessed. Two distinct bugs, found with tools/dpph-history.lua (logs every DPPH/DPPL change with its frame number) and tools/live-slots-diag.lua (tags every out-of-range reference with the frame/DPPH/DPPL/zone that produced it): (1) DPPH holds a bogus boot-time value ($1F, paired with one-off DPPL values $84/$5D) from frame 16 to frame 165 before settling into the real, stable base ($23xx, with DPPL alternating $5D/$A2 every single frame -- a genuine double-buffer, not a bug) -- fixed with a 200-frame settle gate in live-slots.lua (a first attempt at 120 frames wasn't long enough, verified against this same recording before trusting the larger number). (2) A smaller, ongoing torn-read artifact survives the settle fix -- a minority of walked entries (340 of 1072, all landing below $C000, several independently confirmed to fall on already-traced real code when treated as 16K-mirrored ROM addresses) are still garbage on some frames, most likely a genuine emulation-timing race between when the CPU updates a display-list entry and when the once-per-frame Lua callback reads it. Not chased further into MAME's own frame-timing internals -- filtered out instead (discard every reference below $C000, since that's not real ROM space regardless of cause) the same way Centipede's PC-tagged DMA-misattribution reads were filtered by 'impossible as a real address/PC', rather than trusted. The remaining 732 references are dense and consistent across every page from $C000 to $CFFF, and this range holds no already-confirmed code except ENTRY_Nmi's own 3 bytes at $C15F ($C000-$C15E and $C162-$C24C were already-open gaps; sub_C24D and the C300-C361 code block were already correctly traced) -- exactly the shape of a real, contiguous graphics sheet with two small code islands, the same pattern the other two projects' character sheets had. Declared as two blocks either side of what's already correctly traced (rom:C000-rom:C15F is a pre-existing gap not yet block-declared, still open -- see docs/FINDINGS.md for why it wasn't included this pass).
headers.rom:C362: Continuation of the rom:C162 graphics region, resuming after sub_C24D (real code) and the already-confirmed dat_C25C/dat_C25E data and the C300-C361 code block. Ends exactly at $D000 (ENTRY_Reset, real code) with a clean transition -- L_C361's RTS at $C361, then raw zero-padded bytes with no further code or existing labels all the way to $D000. This boundary was already correctly found by the static tracer alone, before any live evidence existed; the live data (dense references throughout) confirms it rather than having been needed to find it.

blocks.name: gfx_C000
blocks.note: CONFIRMED LIVE (43 references, all in the $C078-$C0FE sub-range, tools/live-slots.lua post-fix) plus already-correct static data (dat_C000/C008/C031/C035/C038/C03A/C03B/C04E/C100/C155, each with a real xref) covering the rest -- one block spanning all of it, same family as gfx_C162/gfx_C362, since it's evidently the same resource. Ends exactly where ENTRY_Nmi's 3-byte JMP begins.

blocks.name: gfx_C162
blocks.note: CONFIRMED LIVE (tools/live-slots.lua, run-01.inp, post-fix -- see the header note). Ends where sub_C24D (real code) begins.

blocks.name: gfx_C362
blocks.note: CONFIRMED LIVE (tools/live-slots.lua, run-01.inp, post-fix). Includes the C54A bonus-digit graphics. Ends exactly at ENTRY_Reset ($D000, real code) with no gap -- see the header note.

blocks.name: dat_C25C
blocks.note: CONFIRMED: dat_C25C (2 bytes, xref rom:DA00) and dat_C25E (161 bytes, xref rom:D97E) already rendered correctly as data via the default fallback; declared to stop it showing as an unclaimed gap. Sits between sub_C24D and sub_C300 (both real code).

blocks.name: chr_rom_E000
blocks.note: CONFIRMED three ways: (1) CHARBASE=$E0 by code (rom:D065, rom:DD93, both load #$E0 immediately before the write); (2) gfx.py's default indirect-mode render at --base 0xE000 shows legible 'ATARI' text and a full 0-9 digit set -- see docs/FINDINGS.md; (3) tools/live-slots.lua's post-fix data (30 references) lands entirely within $E000-$E0A8, cleanly avoiding sub_E0C4 (real code, $E0C4-$E0DB) rather than scattering across it the way stale/garbage reads would -- real evidence the walker's indirect-mode handling isn't as suspect here as first worried, not just a coincidence. Checked for the exact bug that bit chr_rom_C000 in the Centipede project before declaring anything: grepped for JSR/JMP into any dat_E0/E1 label, found nothing, so this boundary excludes the code island rather than swallowing it. Starts one byte before CHARBASE's own $E000 base, at $DFFF, because that's where the preceding code (L_DFFE, RTS) actually ends and this data actually begins -- not indicative of anything about CHARBASE itself, MARIA still reads from $E000.

blocks.name: chr_rom_E0DC
blocks.note: Continuation of chr_rom_E000, resuming after sub_E0C4 (real code, ends at $E0DB). Ends where sub_E1E9 (real code) begins. Not yet independently re-checked with a live display-list walk (see rom:E000-family header note in docs/FINDINGS.md on why the walker's indirect-mode handling is itself in question) -- declared on the strength of the code-boundary evidence and the same CHARBASE confirmation, not on a live reference landing specifically in this sub-range.

notes.rom:
Dig Dug (NTSC) (Atari) (1987) (50CB13F3).a78
mapper linear, 16 KB, NTSC
no POKEY declared; audio is the TIA's two voices

Vectors: IRQ $EED8  NMI $C15F  RESET $D000

Written by init.py. Everything here is read from the cartridge; the
judgement calls are yours to add.
